claim: In the tweezers software the laser power is set on a relative scale from 0 to 1, where 1 is the maximum -- about 5 W on the Tweez 305 and about 10 W on the Tweez 310 -- and an internal photodiode's reading of the actual power is shown alongside.

numbers.name: tweez_power_setting_max
numbers.note: the top of the relative scale; the manufacturer calls it the maximum laser power

validity_conditions: Read from Tweez 300 User Manual, 2021 (file date 2022-01-06; sha256 c37027cb..., byte-identical in both places): printed page 24 (PDF page 30). E3 vendor_spec: the manufacturer's statement, not an observation on this bench. The manual is written for the Tweez 305/310 family; this bench's unit is recorded as a Tweez 300 (trapping_laser_identity), and the family naming is the manufacturer's. The approximate maxima are the manual's words. A setting of 0.5 is a fraction of the maximum at the source, not a power at the sample. KNOWLEDGE, NOT POLICY: this is what the manufacturer says. What any session may do, and every limit anyone here acts on, is the person's, written into the envelope after confirming it on the instrument.
